profile.campus: LightEdge Des Moines campus, Altoona, IA (DC1 and DC2, adjacent buildings on Northridge Circle)
profile.reading: LightEdge Des Moines 1, also referred to as DC1, sits at 1435 Northridge Circle in Altoona, Iowa, immediately adjacent to the operator second Des Moines-area building on the same street. Per LightEdge own combined specification sheet for the two-building site, the pair together provide 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load and 10.6 megawatts of total generator capacity with N plus 1 UPS redundancy, across 78,000 total square feet including 40,000 square feet of white space, though the sheet does not break those totals down between DC1 and DC2 individually, so no single-building capacity or square footage figure is assigned to this record. The facility carries a broad compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, PCI DSS, and NIST 800-53 and 800-171 alignment, with ten on-net carriers including Verizon, Lumen, Windstream, and Zayo. LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa, though no formal street address for its headquarters is published on the company own site. LightEdge announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm that also created Digital Realty in 2004, in September 2021, with then-CEO Jim Masterson stating no changes to management, operations, or customer teams as a result. Masterson led the company for 21 years before transitioning to an advisory board role effective the end of 2024, succeeded as CEO by Rob Carter on January 1, 2025. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets, including Kansas City, Omaha, Ashburn, Phoenix, San Jose, and St Louis alongside Des Moines, Austin, San Diego, and Minneapolis, plus a location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named for this specific building. Altoona sits just east of downtown Des Moines and has grown as a suburban technology and light-industrial corridor, a pattern consistent with LightEdge decision to concentrate its Iowa infrastructure there rather than in the city core.

reading.body:
This campus does not publish a single-building power allocation. LightEdge Des Moines 1, also called DC1, occupies one half of a two-building adjacent pair at 1435 Northridge Circle in Altoona that together declare 6.1 megawatts of critical IT load and 10.6 megawatts of generator capacity with N plus 1 UPS redundancy, but the operator's own specification sheet does not separate the capacities between DC1 and DC2, so the IT load available to this individual building is not published.

The certifications on file qualify the campus to host HIPAA and HITECH-regulated workloads, qualified audits under SOC 1, 2, and 3 and ISO 27001, compliance with NIST frameworks 800-53 and 800-171, and PCI DSS cardholder environments. Ten on-net carriers are listed, including Verizon, Lumen, Windstream, and Zayo. No tenant is named for this specific building.

Iowa has 52 mapped data center facilities in the OpenStreetMap record, but only two with published power figures on operator spec pages read by this site, totaling 18 megawatts of declared capacity. This campus ranks third by published megawatts in the state despite that constraint because it and one other facility account for a plurality of Iowa's disclosed supply. Whether the undeclared half of the two-building pair's 6.1 megawatts resides in DC1 or DC2 cannot be determined from the operator's published data.
